The purpose of cascade amplifiers is to increase gain......
You have learned that the voltage gain (Av) of an individual amplifier is as high as 300.
In reality, obtaining gains of that magnitude is not easy. Stability and predictability are lost.
By using an amplifier with a low gain, the circuit is stable and predictable.
However, low gain amplifiers do not amplify the input signal enough to be of practical use.
Using cascade amplifiers, high gain is achieved without losing stability and predictability.7
The overall gain of a cascade amplifier is equal to the product of the individual gains.
For example, the total gain of this cascade amplifier is 1000.
Normally, individual amplifier stages are designed to have a voltage gain of 10.
For example, if a phonograph amplifier needs to amplify the 5 mV output from the record to 5 V to drive a speaker, six stages are needed.

In cascade amplifiers, the output of one amplifier is connected to the input of another amplifier.
There are four methods used to couple one amplifier to another: RC Coupling, LC Coupling, Transformer Coupling and Direct Coupling.
Let's discuss RC coupled cascade amplifiers first. RC Coupling, LC Coupling, Transformer Coupling and Direct Coupling.
Resistance - Capacitance (RC) coupling is the most common method of coupling one stage to the next and uses inexpensive components.
The output signal is developed across collector load resistor (Rc1) and is coupled across the coupling capacitor (Cc2) into the base of the next stage.
The coupling capacitor passes AC signals and blocks DC signals.
In this way, the DC bias levels of one stage do not affect the bias levels of other stages.
The disadvantage of RC coupled amplifiers is the low frequency response.
At low frequencies, the reactance of the coupling capacitor becomes too large, reducing the input and output signals.
RC coupling is used in almost all types of cascade amplifiers except low frequency amplifiers.
In LC coupled amplifiers, the collector load resistor is replaced with an inductor. Inductor - capacitor. RC Coupling, LC Coupling, Transformer Coupling and Direct Coupling.
The coupling capacitors pass AC signals and block DC signals as in RC coupled amplifiers.
However, the inductor acts differently than a collector load resistor.
L1 and L2 have very low resistances to DC. Vcc is applied almost directly to Q1 and Q2 collectors.
L1 and L2 AC resistance depends on the frequency.
At higher frequencies, the reactance is very high, appearing as an open to AC.
The advantage of high AC resistance is that very little AC power is wasted in the inductor. All the AC power is coupled to the next stage.
The disadvantage is the inductors are more expensive than resistors and their reactance drops off at lower frequencies.
Generally, LC coupling is used with radio frequencies (RF). When used in this way, the inductors are called Rf chokes.
Transformer coupling also uses the characteristics of inductance. RC Coupling, LC Coupling, Transformer Coupling and Direct Coupling.
Transformer coupled amplifiers use a transformer and no coupling capacitors. Notice the coupling components in this amplifier circuit.

The output of each stage is connected to the primary windings of T1 and T2.
The inputs to the next stage are taken from the secondary windings of T1 and T2.
The capacitor across the primary of each transformer makes a resonant circuit..rcuit.
This makes the transformers tuned circuits that pass only one frequency.
Transformer coupling is used in radios and TVs. It is the principle behind tuning in a radio station or TV channel.
The disadvantage in using transformer coupling is the size of the transformer at low frequencies.
Transformer coupling is normally used at RF frequencies for radio and TV.
To eliminate the effect that low frequency has on RC, LC and transformer coupling, direct coupling is used. RC Coupling, LC Coupling, Transformer Coupling and Direct Coupling.
In this typical direct coupled cascade amplifier, base biasing resistors are not used. Q1's collector bias is the base bias for Q2.
With no capacitors or inductors used, the amplifiers amplify any signal applied, AC or DC.
The main disadvantage of direct coupling is that transistor characteristics change with temperature and there are no compensating components.
Also, any variation in Vcc, input signal, and emitter to collector current are passed on to the next stage.
Direct coupled amplifiers are used for low frequency applications or when the input frequency extends over a large range of frequencies.
